claims.statement: Let integer-complex reactions y_r->y'_r have jumps nu_r, molecular intensities V k_r(t) phi^V_{y_r}(X^V_{t-}), and a compact positive safe polytope Q in a stoichiometric class with proper relative facets g_i(x)=a_i^T x+b_i>=0. Let predictable allocations satisfy k_t in a nonempty compact coupled set K(X^V_{t-}) subset product_r[0,kbar_r], and suppose for each facet i there are theta_i,eta_i,ell_i>0 such that sup_{x in Q, 0<=g_i(x)<=ell_i, k in K(x)} sum_r k_r x^{y_r}(exp(-theta_i a_i^T nu_r)-1) <= -eta_i. With D_i=sum_r kbar_r E_{y_r}(U)|exp(-theta_i a_i^T nu_r)-1|, any certified C_i>=max(0,sup_{x in Q,k in K(x)} H_i), c_i=theta_i ell_i, V_0=max(1,max_i ceil(2D_i/eta_i)), and any finite activity bound Lambda_Q>=sup_{x in Q,k in K(x)}sum_r k_r x^{y_r}, every compatible initial lattice point X_0^V in Q and every predictable admissible allocation obey, for V>=V_0 and finite T, P(tau_Q<=T) <= sum_i exp(-theta_i V g_i(X_0^V)) + T sum_i (V C_i+D_i)exp(-c_i V). The result is a conditional candidate theorem: it follows from the exact molecular generator, the uniform falling-factorial correction, and a stopped exponential-potential/Dynkin argument; it does not imply infinite-time survival or stochastic permanence.
assumptions: Each reaction has integer nonnegative molecular complexes and uses the stated falling-factorial mass-action convention; factorial divisors are absorbed into k_r.
Q is compact, lies in the strictly positive orthant and in the supplied affine stoichiometric class; all remaining inequalities are proper relative facets and coordinate bounds U are supplied.
K(x) is nonempty compact and contained in the per-reaction box [0,kbar]; the control is predictable, including any dependence on time, past history, or independent randomness.
The coupled exponential-generator collar inequality is globally certified for every facet and every feasible allocation, not merely sampled on trajectories.
The initial count is on the required integer reaction-lattice/coset and belongs to Q; the result's volume threshold uses the exact finite-volume correction D_i.

claims.novelty_boundary: This is an application-facing refinement of the pinned N35 finite-volume exit theorem. The support-function test preserves coupled feasible flux constraints instead of relaxing them to an independent per-reaction rate box. Exponential supermartingales, controlled finite-state reachability and chemical-network large deviations are established ingredients. No exhaustive priority search, external proof review, real metabolic network validation or practical acquisition algorithm was completed; do not claim novelty or a biological result.

initial count, compatible conservation totals and integer reaction-lattice coset
isotope-tracing or other flux inequalities coupling pathways
ATP/redox/transport turnover and uptake, secretion, dilution, and degradation boundary terms
time-stamped allocation/intervention logs defining the predictable control envelope
costs.certificate_computation: For fixed x the support maximization in k is an LP; global collar and full-Q certification requires rational interval subdivision or real-algebraic optimization and can be exponential in dimension. Once certificates are supplied, constants and bound evaluation use O(mR) facet/reaction terms.

claims.falsifier: The algebraic certificate is rejected by any feasible (x,k) in a declared collar with H_i(x,k;theta_i)>-eta_i, or by an exact finite-volume CTMC/control computation whose exit probability exceeds the claimed right-hand side. A physical falsifier is a replicated first-exit frequency whose valid lower confidence bound exceeds the bound after validating initial counts, volume, stoichiometry, pool conservation, flux-set membership, propensity law and observation error.
claims.next_gate: Acquire a small closed or explicitly budgeted metabolic subnetwork with public or newly measured enzyme/flux constraints; verify the conservation ledger and count coset; globally certify a coupled collar; compare against an equally informed independent-box certificate and exact finite-state Bellman reachability at small V. Continue only if the coupled certificate produces a material held-out risk/exponent improvement.

claims.statement: For 2A->A+B and 2B->A+B with A+B=V, x=A/V, Q=[1/4,3/4], collar width 1/32 and the coupled allocation K={(q,q):1<=q<=16}, the deterministic collar drift margin is 7/16. The theta=1/2 exponential-generator test has margin eta=3/20; rigorous rational Taylor enclosures certify the chosen upper bound C_i=109/20, D_i=2086/125, V_0=223, c_i=1/64, and Lambda_Q=10. From A_0=B_0=1500 at V=3000, the theorem gives P(tau_Q<=exp(23.4375)) approximately 2.16877191e-6, hence below 2.17e-6. Replacing K by the independent box [1,16]^2 fails the collar condition: at x=1/4 and (k_A,k_B)=(16,1), the drift is exactly -7/16 and the rational theta=1/2 generator lower bound is H_L>1470431/3440640>0. The exact-rational verifier passes all rational inequalities and this comparator witness; decimal exponentials are used only for printed numerical diagnostics.
assumptions: The coupled allocation equality k_A=k_B is an actual measured/control constraint and every q in [1,16] is admissible.
Molecular propensities are exactly V k_A (A)_2/V^2 and V k_B (B)_2/V^2, with the count total A+B=V closed and conserved.
The starting count is exactly (1500,1500) at V=3000; the prediction concerns the stated model time units and polytope exit event.
